input.title: The Analytics Engine persists to exactly three tables joined many-to-many

input.description: AnalyticsSeries holds raw values, AnalyticsDimension holds dimensions, and AnalyticsSeries_AnalyticsDimension is the lookup table. The browser store creates all three in PGlite itself.

input.content:
The whole storage model is three tables:

- **`AnalyticsSeries`** — the raw values: `source`, `start`, `end`, `metric`, `value`, `unit`, `fn`, `params`.
- **`AnalyticsDimension`** — the dimension records: `dimension`, `path`, plus display metadata (`label`, `icon`, `description`).
- **`AnalyticsSeries_AnalyticsDimension`** — the many-to-many lookup joining the two, indexed on both `seriesId` and `dimensionId`.

The many-to-many join is the point, not an implementation detail. There will be millions of series rows and only a handful of distinct dimension rows, so dimensions are *shared* decorations rather than columns on the series. That is what lets a query aggregate *across* unrelated series that happen to share a dimension path, which is the capability the engine exists to provide.

The series table is heavily indexed — `start`, `end`, `metric`, `source`, `unit`, `value`, and `fn` each get their own index — which is why filtered time-window queries stay cheap and why arbitrary post-hoc SQL is deliberately not exposed on the interface.

Provisioning differs by store. `BrowserAnalyticsStore.init()` runs a `create table if not exists` script inside PGlite, so it is self-provisioning and idempotent — you never migrate it by hand. The Postgres store assumes a fully initialized database and ships an init script instead; it will not create the schema for you.

Provenance: draft `03-Build/04-WorkWithData/_06-Analytics Engine/typescript/schema.md`; DDL verified in the `initSql` block of `packages/analytics-engine/browser/src/BrowserAnalyticsStore.ts` at 6.2.2-dev.45. The draft attributes the auto-create behaviour to a `browser` package built on `MemoryAnalyticsStore`; the class has since been folded into `BrowserAnalyticsStore`.

The whole storage model is three tables — re-verified against the DDL at 6.2.2-dev.45, and it is still exactly three:

- **`AnalyticsSeries`** — the raw values: `source`, `start`, `end`, `metric`, `value`, `unit`, `fn`, `params`.
- **`AnalyticsDimension`** — the dimension records: `dimension`, `path`, plus display metadata (`label`, `icon`, `description`).
- **`AnalyticsSeries_AnalyticsDimension`** — the many-to-many lookup joining the two, indexed on both `seriesId` and `dimensionId`.

Nothing else is created, and no persisted database view exists either — `KnexAnalyticsStore._buildViewQuery` builds an *inline* subquery aliased `AV` at query time, so "view" in that code is a SQL expression, not a fourth schema object.

The many-to-many join is the point, not an implementation detail. There will be millions of series rows and only a handful of distinct dimension rows, so dimensions are *shared* decorations rather than columns on the series. That is what lets a query aggregate *across* unrelated series that happen to share a dimension path, which is the capability the engine exists to provide.

Both foreign keys in the join table are `on delete cascade`, and that is what shapes the store interface. Deleting series rows (`clearSeriesBySource`) silently takes the join rows with them but leaves the `AnalyticsDimension` rows behind as orphans, because dimensions are shared and no single series owns one. Hence the second, separately callable `clearEmptyAnalyticsDimensions()` on `IAnalyticsStore`, and hence the optional `cleanUpDimensions` flag on `clearSeriesBySource` that just chains the two. The apparently redundant pair of methods is a direct consequence of the schema shape.

The series table is heavily indexed — `start`, `end`, `metric`, `source`, `unit`, `value`, and `fn` each get their own index — which is why filtered time-window queries stay cheap and why arbitrary post-hoc SQL is deliberately not exposed on the interface.

Provisioning differs by store, and the DDL is physically duplicated. `BrowserAnalyticsStore.init()` runs a `create table if not exists` script (the `initSql` template literal in its own source file) inside PGlite, so it is self-provisioning and idempotent — you never migrate it by hand. `PostgresAnalyticsStore` will not create the schema for you: it assumes an initialized database, and the init script that creates it lives in a *different package*, as `initAnalyticsStoreSql` in `packages/reactor-api/src/utils/db.ts`, which `reactor-api`'s server loops over via `knex.raw` at startup. The two copies are currently byte-identical apart from being one string versus an array of strings, but they are maintained separately — worth knowing if you ever see the two environments disagree about a column. Note also that there are no Knex migration files for these tables anywhere in the monorepo; the only provisioning path is one of these two raw-SQL scripts.

Provenance: draft `03-Build/04-WorkWithData/_06-Analytics Engine/typescript/schema.md`. DDL verified in the `initSql` block of `packages/analytics-engine/browser/src/BrowserAnalyticsStore.ts` and in `initAnalyticsStoreSql` at `packages/reactor-api/src/utils/db.ts:175`; table set cross-checked against every table reference in `packages/analytics-engine/knex/src/KnexAnalyticsStore.ts` at 6.2.2-dev.45. The draft attributes the auto-create behaviour to a `browser` package built on a `MemoryAnalyticsStore` base class; that class does not exist anywhere in the source (`git grep MemoryAnalyticsStore` returns zero hits outside the academy docs), and `BrowserAnalyticsStore` carries the DDL itself.

_Source-verified 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse source at v6.2.2-dev.45._

input.description: AnalyticsSeries holds raw values, AnalyticsDimension holds dimensions, AnalyticsSeries_AnalyticsDimension is the cascade-deleting lookup. DDL is duplicated in browser and reactor-api.
